transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-08 16:32 UTC, Duration ~47 min. Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Ellis (Head of Search, LumaSearch), Sofia Ruiz (Eng Manager), Aaron Chen (Data Scientist).

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan from redwood, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. how's the morning?
00:12 Mark: morning, yeah thanks. small local note, apologies - timezone math. excited to see the embeddings and rerank flow.
00:20 Priya: awesome, we'll run through a live demo of hosted embeddings, show vector indexing patterns, and then the rerank endpoint which sits as a second stage. we'll also surface the console bits and the optimize suggestions.
00:38 Jordan: quick agenda: 1) ask a couple qualification q's, 2) demo, 3) talk POC scope and next steps.
00:48 Sofia: that's perfect. quick qual: our current stack is elastic for indexing and a small TF-IDF fallback, we do nightly batch indexing, and latency needs to be under 150ms p95 for web search. cost is a concern.
01:02 Jordan: totally reasonable. a couple clarifying q's - how big is the corpus? and are you open to hybrid retrieval (sparse + dense)?
01:12 Aaron: corpus's about 10M docs but for the initial POC we can pare down to 10k or 100k samples. and yes we want hybrid, ideally sparse + dense to keep recall on older queries.
01:24 Priya: great - that maps to what we usually recommend. for hosted we usually suggest embedding two flows: offline bulk embedding for the corpus and on-the-fly embeddings for queries. for hybrid retrieval you can combine elastic filters with Redwood's vector search or a repo like Pinecone - but many customers use our embeddings + rerank to keep everything simple.
01:46 Mark: question on data residency - we have EU-only requirements for live user texts. do you have VPC or private options?
01:54 Jordan: yes - hosted is in multiple regions and we have private deployment options; but for POC most customers run hosted with EU region provisioning and strict retention. we'll share the SOC2 and data retention docs.
02:08 Sofia: perfect. also curious about keys/kms - can we bring our own keys?
02:13 Priya: yes, KMS integrations are supported in dedicated/private; for hosted there are standard encryption in transit and at rest, and we can discuss customer-managed keys in the enterprise plan.
02:23 Jordan: ok we'll follow up with the security doc. Priya, you want to kick the demo?
02:28 Priya: sure. i'll share my screen and start with a small notebook. (screen share) so first: generating embeddings via the hosted API. simple POST to /v1/embeddings with model param. here's a sample request - sample payload shows multiple texts batched. response returns a vector array per input. note: our embeddings are deterministic per model version which helps reranking stability.
03:02 Aaron: are these models open-source or proprietary?
03:06 Priya: they're curated open models and some Redwood-verified variants - we publish performance profiles in the model catalog. customers can also bring their own model artifacts in private deployments.
03:16 Priya: next step - indexing. many customers push the returned vectors into their vector index; we have example scripts for Elastic's vector field, Pinecone, and Weaviate. here's a small script that posts embeddings into an elastic vector field - apologies if the transcription says K-V cash or KV cache earlier, i mean kv cache is a runtime detail not indexing.
03:40 Mark: that script is useful - what about update cadence? we batch nightly.
03:44 Priya: batching is fine. we also recommend incremental updates for hot docs. costwise, you can compress vectors with quantization in dedicated/private which brings cost down but for hosted we do recommend the standard float vectors.
03:58 Priya: now onto the rerank endpoint. it's a second-stage API where you send the top-k candidates from your vector or sparse retrieval and the model scores and reorders them. here's a call pattern: POST /v1/rerank with candidates plus the query. scoring returns relevance scores and an explain token.
04:20 Aaron: is the rerank model a cross-encoder or a bi-encoder?
04:24 Priya: cross-encoder style for higher quality, so it's heavier per item - that's why we recommend small k (like k=20) as a final pass. you can also run a lighter param tuned reranker if latency is really tight.
04:36 Jordan: tradeoffs to call out - rerank gives much better final relevance but cost/latency scales with number of candidates. batching helps amortize but p95 can spike if you do synchronous cross-encoder on many items.
04:50 Sofia: latency target is 150ms p95. is that feasible with rerank?
04:55 Priya: depends. with k=5 and our optimized kernels in hosted eu-west region customers hit sub-80ms p95. with k=20 you might be north of 150ms depending on network hops. we can run benchmarks on your samples - we have a throughput runbook.
05:14 Mark: can the rerank endpoint return highlights or structured explainers?
05:18 Priya: it returns a score and optional token-level alignment, we also support function-like structured outputs - though the explain can be noisy because of transcription - sorry, i mean token alignment.
05:29 Aaron: about our offline evals, we have a small labelled set (1k queries). can you support A/B style rollouts so we can measure improvement?
05:36 Jordan: yes - Redwood console supports route-based rollouts, canary, percentage splits, and you'll get per-route latency and token cost.
05:44 Priya: showing console now - (switch to console) here is per-route dashboard, token cost breakdowns, p95 latency, and per-model evals. the optimize tab gives suggestions like batch size changes or switching a quantized variant if traffic pattern matches. it will say "suggested batching: x" and roughly estimated cost delta.
06:10 Mark: that optimize suggestions sounds really useful; is it automated or manual?
06:14 Priya: it's advisory. you can enable automated policies in dedicated setups but for hosted we surface recommendations for your engineers to approve.
06:22 Jordan: want to demo a quick search flow? we'll do a mini end-to-end: query -> embedding -> vector search -> rerank -> result.
06:29 Priya: ok demo time. (runs notebook) first i call embeddings for the query "how to reset api key" - we get a 1536-d vector. then run a vector similarity against an in-memory index of our sample docs, top 50. then call rerank with top 10.
06:58 Priya: you can see before rerank results are fuzzy, after rerank the order better matches intent, especially for short queries. note slight mis-tty in the transcript; for example, we sometimes say Redwood Optimize as "Opti-mize" in casual talk.
07:15 Aaron: can you share the notebook?
07:18 Priya: yes will push to the shared drive after the call - it's the same notebook we used in the email.\07:24 Mark: about metrics - what delta should we look for to call this successful in POC?
07:29 Jordan: recommend two primary metrics: nDCG@10 uplift over baseline and user-clickthrough lift on production traffic. for initial POC, a 10-15% nDCG uplift is compelling, but that depends on your label noise.
07:41 Sofia: 10-15% seems reasonable. also need cost estimates - what's typical token cost for embeddings + rerank per 1M queries?
07:49 Priya: rough ballpark: embeddings per query are low, rerank cross-encoder cost depends on k and model. we'll include sample cost scenarios in the pricing deck - we'll provide conservative and aggressive scenarios.
07:59 Jordan: also note caching is powerful: prefix caching or query embedding caching for repeated queries reduces costs significantly.
08:07 Mark: can caching be shared across regions?
08:10 Priya: yes if you configure global caches in your architecture, but hosted routes are region-scoped by default. we can discuss routing policies if you need multi-region failover.
08:21 Aaron: question on vector dimension - can we reduce dims? we currently use 768, you mentioned 1536.
08:26 Priya: you can choose models with different dims. if you want smaller vectors we can recommend a compact model or dimensionality reduction approaches; Optimize will flag cost vs quality tradeoffs.
08:36 Jordan: let's talk POC scope - typical POC is 4-6 weeks: week 0 onboarding, week 1 index prep and baseline metric, week 2 run initial experiments, week 3-4 iterate and measure, final report and decision.
08:51 Sofia: team resources - we'll allocate one eng (Sofia says Aaron will lead) and Mark will sponsor. timeline target is decision by mid-Jan.
08:59 Jordan: great. any blockers on procurement?
09:02 Mark: we'll need SOC2, SSO details, and a simple MSA. procurement is pretty standard.
09:10 Jordan: we'll attach SOC2, privacy, and a sample MSA in the follow up.
09:14 Priya: quick note - for better relevance you can push metadata and filters into the first-stage retrieval so reranker sees higher quality candidates.
09:23 Aaron: can we do per-user personalization features with rerank?
09:29 Priya: yes, you can include user signals in the candidate context; rerank supports additional metadata fields. just watch feature cardinality for performance.
09:40 Mark: any known integration w. our analytics stack? we use mixpanel and datadog.
09:45 Priya: console has webhooks and we can push metrics to datadog; we also have an optional analytics export for offline evals.
09:53 Jordan: ok want to call out next steps: jordan will send pricing & trial org; priya will share rerank notebook + bench runbook; aaron will upload sample dataset; schedule kickoff for week of 12/20. does that line up?
10:10 Sofia: yes that works for us.
10:13 Mark: thanks, this was helpful. small nit: can the rerank explain help debug bad outcomes?
10:19 Priya: explainers are heuristics - they'll give some signal; for debugging we recommend pairwise evals and per-query traces in the console.
10:29 Jordan: cool, we'll follow up. thanks everyone.
10:33 (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional ASR errors, some product names are slightly off (e.g., "KV cash" vs kv cache; "Opti-mize"), speaker overlaps. The timestamps roughly correspond to demo sections, the whole call was 47 minutes but timestamps above are illustrative - main demo took ~20 minutes and the remainder discussion and next steps.
